issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 3.4 claims that the bilinear form \mathcal{A}_h(\bmf{\Phi}; \cdot, I_h^* \cdot) = a_h(\cdot, I_h^* \cdot) + b_h(\bmf{\Phi}; \cdot, I_h^* \cdot) is symmetric up to O(h). However, the gyromagnetic form b(\bmf{\Phi}; \bmf{u}, \bmf{v}) = \int_\Omega (\bmf{\Phi} \times \nabla \bmf{u}) \cdot \nabla \bmf{v} is skew-symmetric, satisfying b(\bmf{\Phi}; \bmf{u}, \bmf{v}) - b(\bmf{\Phi}; \bmf{v}, \bmf{u}) = 2 b(\bmf{\Phi}; \bmf{u}, \bmf{v}), which is generically of order O(1). Its FVEM discretization b_h approximates this skew-symmetric form, so |b_h(\bmf{\Phi}; \tilde{\bmf{m}}_h, I_h^* \bmf{v}_h) - b_h(\bmf{\Phi}; \bmf{v}_h, I_h^* \tilde{\bmf{m}}_h)| does not vanish at rate O(h). In Appendix C, the proof bounds the difference between continuous and discrete forms against an auxiliary function \tilde{\bmf{m}} \in \bmf{H}^2, completely omitting the O(1) skew-symmetric component 2 b(\bmf{\Phi}; \tilde{\bmf{m}}_h, \bmf{v}_h).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish an H^1 energy estimate for the auxiliary problem without assuming almost-symmetry of the skew-symmetric gyromagnetic term in the FVEM setting.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.4 is false. Consequently, the H^1 error estimate in Proposition 3.5 fails because it relies directly on Lemma 3.4 to bound \mathcal{A}_h(\bmf{\Phi}; \bmf{\xi}, I_h^* \partial_t \bmf{\xi}) by C h \|\bmf{\xi}\|_{H^1} \|\partial_t \bmf{\xi}\|_{H^1} and absorb it via an inverse inequality.
issues.title: False almost-symmetry estimate for non-symmetric FVEM bilinear form
issues.why_classification: Lemma 3.4 is mathematically false, and repairing the H^1 error bound of the non-symmetric parabolic FVEM auxiliary system requires a fundamentally different analysis technique rather than a local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem 3.6 attempts to bound \bmf{m} - \bmf{m}_h by passing through an iteration sequence \tilde{\bmf{m}}^l and \tilde{\bmf{m}}_h^l. However: (1) Lemma 3.2 only asserts that successive iterates of a single-step backward Euler scheme with step \tau satisfy \|\tilde{\bmf{m}}^{l+1} - \tilde{\bmf{m}}^l\|_{H^2} \to 0$; it does not prove convergence to the continuous-in-time exact solution \bmf{m}(t). (2) Setting \bmf{\Phi} = \tilde{\bmf{m}}_h^l in the linear auxiliary scheme (3.7) does not make it equivalent to the nonlinear scheme (2.7), and no argument is given that \tilde{\bmf{m}}_h^l converges to \bmf{m}_h. (3) Applying Proposition 3.5 with \bmf{\Phi} = \tilde{\bmf{m}}_h^l violates the premise \bmf{\Phi} \in \bmf{X} \subset L^\infty(0,T; \bmf{H}^2), since piecewise linear finite volume element functions \tilde{\bmf{m}}_h^l \in \bmf{S}_h$ are not in \bmf{H}^2.

issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem 3.6 fails entirely; the spatial error bounds \|\bmf{m} - \bmf{m}_h\|_{L^2} \leq C h^2$ and \|\bmf{m} - \bmf{m}_h\|_{H^1} \leq C h for the Landau-Lifshitz equation are left unproved.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition 3.10 assumes that the continuous piecewise linear finite volume element solution \bmf{m}_h \in \bmf{S}_h$ satisfies |\bmf{m}_h(\bmf{x})| = 1 pointwise for all \bmf{x} \in \Omega. An affine vector field on a triangle whose magnitude is constant 1 is necessarily spatially constant (as the sphere contains no line segments); thus no non-trivial discrete solution \bmf{m}_h can ever satisfy this hypothesis. Furthermore, in the proof, testing (3.14) with I_h^* \partial_t \bmf{m}_h produces terms such as (\bmf{m}_h \times \partial_t \bmf{m}_h, I_h^* \partial_t \bmf{m}_h) and (|\nabla \bmf{m}_h|^2 \bmf{m}_h, I_h^* \partial_t \bmf{m}_h). Because I_h^* \partial_t \bmf{m}_h$ is piecewise constant on dual cells while \bmf{m}_h varies within each dual cell, these Petrov-Galerkin pairings do not vanish, and the deduction of energy dissipation fails.

issues.title: Impossible pointwise unit length hypothesis and invalid cancellations in discrete energy dissipation
issues.why_classification: The result relies on an impossible hypothesis for non-trivial continuous piecewise linear functions and ignores non-vanishing cross terms in the Petrov-Galerkin weak formulation, defeating the primary stability claim.
